### Report Merging — Bug Fixes

- **Merged Reports No Longer Repeat the Test Suite Name.** When merging several already-generated reports from the same test suite (e.g. re-running different subsets of tests and merging the resulting reports), the Test Suite name previously appeared once per merged-in report instead of once for the whole merged document. It now appears once, in both PDF and Word merges.
- **Merge Order Now Matches Execution Order, and Can Be Reordered.** The Merge Reports dialog previously combined reports most-recently-generated-first, which could reverse the order the test suites were actually run in (e.g. the last suite run would appear first in the merged report). Reports are now merged oldest-generated-first by default, and a new Move Up/Down control lets you set a different order before merging.

### Header Logos in Merged Reports

- **Merge Reports Now Has TocMode and HeaderLogo Fields.** The Merge Reports dialog now includes the same TocMode and HeaderLogo fields already available in the report editor, so a merged report's rebuilt Table of Contents/List of Figures can carry your own header logo. Choosing TocMode "none" disables the HeaderLogo field, since no new TOC page is built in that mode.
- **Header Logo Now Appears on Merged Word Reports.** Word (DOCX) reports previously had no header logo support at all, even though the field existed in the report editor. Merging Word reports now embeds the header logo once on the merged output's header, and every merged section correctly inherits it.
- **Fixed: Header Logo Was Missing From the Table of Contents/List of Figures.** A defect in how the logo was placed onto a page caused it to be silently clipped away once the page was finalized - most noticeable on the Table of Contents and List of Figures pages, which never showed a logo at all. This is now fixed for every page, in both PDF and Word output.
- **Fixed: Long Header Text Could Overlap the Header Logo.** Header text is now wrapped so it never runs into the logo, instead of the two overlapping.
- **Header Logos Now Render Crisp Instead of Blurry.** Header logos (PNG, JPG, SVG, and PDF) are no longer rasterized by the plotting engine - they're embedded directly into the final report when it's generated or merged, so SVG and PDF logos stay fully vector/crisp at any zoom level.
